whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the AFC-320 §0.10.5 evidence-run bundle: tests/db/69_retention_evidence_run.sql (suite 'evidence', 24 assertions). Coder is the author of both paths listed below. This claim asserts authorship and paths; it asserts nothing about whether the change is correct. R2 is pending: tests/db/** sits on REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS, and the designated reviewer for a Coder compliance-path commit is the CTO (MediaTech). The review is requested on AFC-320; on approval the commit will carry a truthful Reviewed-by: MediaTech (CTO) trailer naming that decision. No trailer is written before the review actually happens. There is no independent security reviewer on this team -- that seat was declined by the board on cost -- so a CTO review of this compliance-path change is a recorded degradation, not independent review.
whatTheChangeDoes: Adds suite 69, the repeatable evidence-run bundle for plan §0.10.5: two synthetic fixture persons under policy fixture.medical v1 (inserted idempotently ON CONFLICT (rule_key, version), so the bundle neither depends on suite 61 nor forks the rule), both with genuinely due clocks (closed concern 3 years ago against a 1-year floor, asserted as instants per AFC-202); a LIVE retention.run('scheduler:retention-nightly', 'live') executed as retention_job via SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION (the suite-67 technique, never SET ROLE); assertions that the due row went 1 -> 0 with manifest action='deleted', the run recorded succeeded/live with actor='retention_job' and the scheduler string as label only, the person row surviving (D3); and a held-clock negative control (person-scoped hold on the second fixture) asserting the row survived with manifest skipped/held and clock state 'held'. A final block emits the run header and both items as AFC_EVIDENCE/1 notices, which the harness ledger ignores by design and a capture script reads off the notice stream. No engine, bootstrap, migration, harness, or gate file is touched.
whyNotGrandfathered: Neither exemption file is used. scripts/r2-grandfathered.json is untouched: the R2 review is being obtained for real from the CTO on AFC-320, not grandfathered away. No rollback-control question arises: no migration is added or changed.

Manifest capture: a throwaway replay script (kept in run scratch, NOT committed) applied the identical load order -- bootstrap, migrations, engine, assert.sql, suites 10..69 -- kept the database open, and read back the evidence run: retention_runs row (mode live, status succeeded, actor retention_job, actor_label scheduler:retention-nightly) plus the fixture_medical item (action deleted, no skip reason) and the control item (action skipped, skip_reason held). The same run header carries counts {deleted: 2, skipped: 51, held: 15, would_delete: 0, indeterminate: 20, failed: 0}; the second 'deleted' is the engine marking the erasure fixture's due fixture_forge clock, for which no target row existed -- the bundle's proven real deletion is the fixture_medical item with the 1 -> 0 row count, and the comment says so. PG_URL execution was not run: no non-prod postgres exists yet (parent AFC-267 owns provisioning), and the dev sandbox has no container runtime or PG server binaries. PG_URL-readiness rests on construction, stated in the suite header: no PGlite-only behaviour, no absolute dates, instant (not rendering) comparisons, SESSION AUTHORIZATION restore spelled per the suite-67 convention, idempotent policy insert, own fixtures only.

reviews.findings: All four R2 checks pass, verified on this tree 2026-10-09. (1) Scope: git show --stat 308e910 touches exactly 2 new files, tests/db/69_retention_evidence_run.sql + .provenance/claims/AFC-320.json; no engine, bootstrap, migration, harness, or gate change. (2) Harness green: node scripts/run-db-tests.mjs -> 17 suites passed, 0 failed, 590 assertions, 0 failing (suite 69 [evidence] contributes its 24); retention-literal-gate.sh exit 0. (3) Technique: the live call is retention.run('scheduler:retention-nightly','live') as retention_job via SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION with session-identity + non-superuser preconditions asserted and harness identity restored before read-back (suite-67 convention, RESET avoided per PGlite 0.2.17 note); held-clock negative control present -- same run erases the due fixture (1->0, manifest deleted) and spares the held fixture (manifest skipped/held, clock 'held'); D3 person-row survival asserted; attribution asserted as session actor with scheduler string as label only. (4) Synthetic fixtures only: bodies are labels, DOBs generic 50-year offsets, no real personal data. Testing-strategy lens: the held control is what makes this evidence rather than a self-fulfilling erasure. Security lens: least-privilege impersonation (SESSION AUTHORIZATION, never SET ROLE from superuser) is asserted, not trusted. STANDING DEGRADATION: there is no independent security reviewer on this team (board declined the seat on cost); this CTO review of a compliance-path commit is a recorded degradation, not independent review.
